final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim using the same record. That narrowing is substantively valid as an interpretation: the current evidence supports a disclosure-dependent theory more than a clean-certification theory. But that is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats on this record, because the key compliance predicate is not merely acknowledging that disclosure is required; it is evidence that the required disclosure has actually been made, or that approved risk acceptance exists, or that the weakness has been remediated. None of those facts is in evidence. Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support release-level readiness, and public guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring residual risk, but those points do not satisfy the internal policy condition that controls certification status. The unresolved concern therefore remains a missing support link, not cured by reframing alone.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required limitation disclosure has actually been incorporated into the final model card or launch materials for the named launch use case.
The aviation maintenance triage slice remains below target in deferred-defect routing, so a live material weakness still exists on this record.
The mitigation artifact remains a draft runbook with TBD owner and alert threshold, so it does not satisfy the policy predicate for certification without material caveats.
The model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations remains in tension with the unresolved slice issue and the disclosure policy.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved weakness before launch.
